acceptance_criteria.criterion: The credentials table in settings renders columns: Label, Host, Token, Actions.
The add credential form includes a required "Label" field, with Host and Token fields, and button text "Add Credential".
Clicking "Edit" on a credential row enables inline editing of Label and Token fields; Host is read-only.
Clicking "Save" after inline editing calls PUT /api/config/credentials with the existing credential id and updated fields.
Delete button calls DELETE /api/config/credentials/:id (by credential id, not host).

When deleting a credential referenced by repositories, the confirmation dialog warns: "Remove credential '{label}'? {N} repository/repositories currently use this credential and will lose their credential association."
When deleting a credential not referenced by any repository, the confirmation dialog shows: "Remove credential '{label}' for host '{host}'? This action cannot be undone."
api.config.credentials.add() sends PUT /api/config/credentials with the correct body (no id).
api.config.credentials.update(id, data) sends PUT /api/config/credentials with the existing id in the body.
All GUI tests in settings.test.mjs and api.config.test.mjs pass.

summary: Updated api.js credentials namespace: renamed set()→add(), added update(id, data) sending PUT with id in body, renamed delete(host)→remove(id) sending DELETE /api/config/credentials/:id.

Updated settings.js buildTableHead() to emit Label, Host, Token, Actions columns. Rewrote buildCredentialRow() to accept a credential object {id, label, host, maskedToken}, add Label cell with inline edit input, Token cell with password input for edit mode, host cell always read-only, Edit/Save/Cancel action buttons, and delete flow that fetches repositories to check for references and builds the correct confirmation message.
Updated buildAddCredentialForm() to include a required Label field before Host, changed submit button text to 'Add Credential', calls api.config.credentials.add().
Updated renderCredentialsTable() to iterate over an array (not Object.entries) of credential objects.

Updated settings.test.mjs: corrected AC3 tests for new data shape (array vs object), added AC-T1 through AC-T7 tests covering new column headers, add form label field, inline edit mode, save calls update with id, remove called with id not host, and delete confirmation message variants.
Updated api.config.test.mjs: added structure, list, add, update, and remove tests verifying correct HTTP method, URL, and body shape for all new credential API client methods.
All 17 settings.test.mjs and 23 api.config.test.mjs tests pass. Other test suites unaffected.

comments.note: settings.js buildCredentialRow(): the cred object passed to the row builder is the same reference returned from api.config.credentials.list(). Mutating cred.label on save works but creates an implicit coupling between the list cache and the row state. Consider returning a new credential object from the update call and re-rendering the row, or using a local state variable for the current label to avoid this coupling. Not a bug — noted as a design observation.

settings.js: the enter/escape keydown handler is only attached to labelInput, not to tokenInput. Adding an equivalent handler on tokenInput would improve keyboard UX (consistent with the repositories inline-edit pattern which attaches the handler to its single input). Out of WP-008 scope but worth noting.

api.config.test.mjs: the test file previously had no tests for api.config.credentials — the old set()/delete(host) methods were untested. This debt is now addressed by the new add/update/remove tests added in WP-008.

settings.test.mjs: showConfirm (ESM export from confirm-dialog.js) cannot be easily monkey-patched in the Node test environment without dynamic import tricks. The AC-T6/AC-T7 tests verify the message-building logic indirectly by checking the repositories mock and expected message format rather than intercepting the confirm dialog call. This is consistent with the existing test approach in the file and is acceptable, but worth noting for future test infrastructure improvements.

comments.note: settings.js buildCredentialRow() saveBtn handler (line 183): no client-side validation guard for empty label before calling api.config.credentials.update(). A user can save an empty string as the label — the server should reject this, but adding a client-side isEmpty check would match the pattern used in the Add form (validateRequired). Not an AC requirement but worth addressing in a follow-up.

settings.js buildCredentialRow(): Enter/Escape keydown handler is attached to labelInput only, not tokenInput. Pressing Enter in the token field during inline edit does not trigger Save. The repositories.js inline-edit pattern attaches the handler to its single input — consistency would attach it to tokenInput too. Pre-existing observation from Developer; out of WP-008 scope.

notes-collected.test.mjs hangs (process does not exit) — pre-existing issue, file not modified by WP-008 (git status and git diff both clean for this file). Likely a dangling async handle or timer stub in the test setup. Should be investigated independently.

summary: [PASS] Code review complete. No blocking issues found across all four modified files. Implementation is clean, idiomatic, and consistent with established codebase patterns.

comments.note: api.js credentials.update(id, data): the spread { id, ...data } is correctly ordered — the explicit id is not overridable by the data argument. This is the right pattern. No change needed; noting for future reference when adding other credential fields.

settings.js buildCredentialRow() deleteBtn handler: the 'Deleting…' spinner state is only applied after showConfirm resolves (correct — no point disabling the button during the dialog). On success the row is removed from the DOM via onDeleted() re-render, so there is no need to reset the button state on success. The error branch correctly resets it. Behavior is correct.

settings.js buildCredentialRow(): the defensive dual-key check `r.credentialId || r.CredentialId` in the delete flow correctly mirrors the project-wide API response normalisation convention documented in the ProjectResponse typedef (Go-capitalised vs lowercase keys). Good defensive coding aligned with the codebase pattern.

settings.test.mjs AC-T5: the test calls api.config.credentials.remove(credId) directly rather than simulating the full click-flow, due to the ESM export constraint on showConfirm. The comment in the test file honestly explains this limitation. The indirect approach is consistent with how AC-T6 and AC-T7 also validate logic indirectly. This is an acceptable trade-off for the current test infrastructure.

api.config.test.mjs structure test verifies that all four credential method names (list, add, update, remove) exist as functions. This is a useful regression guard against accidental future renames breaking callers. Pattern is consistent with the existing polling and notesDisplay structure tests.

[documentation-forward] settings.js buildCredentialRow(): the JSDoc @param for 'onDeleted' says 'Callback to refresh the table after deletion.' — this could be expanded to clarify that onDeleted() triggers a full re-render of the credentials table (calls renderCredentialsTable internally) and is invoked only on successful delete, not on error or cancel. Helps future contributors understand the refresh-on-delete lifecycle.

[documentation-forward] settings.js buildCredentialsSection() JSDoc: the @returns comment says '{{ element: HTMLElement }}' but does not mention that calling this function also triggers the initial async table load as a side-effect (renderCredentialsTable is called synchronously inside the factory). The function-level JSDoc already notes this in prose but the @returns shape comment could include a 'Side-effect' callout for inline-edit readers. Low priority — the prose description covers it adequately.

[documentation-forward] api.js credentials.update() @param for 'data': the JSDoc lists { label?: string, token?: string } but does not note that omitting token means the server retains the existing token unchanged — this is implied by the settings.js implementation (tokenInput left blank = no token key in updateData) but is not explicit in the API client docs. Adding a note 'Omit token to leave the existing token unchanged' would help callers.
